proposals.relationship: Le Goff credits Bloch’s combination of intellectual structure and medieval erudition as a resource for his formation and later endorses his analysis of complex social arrangements.
proposals.evidence_note: Le Goff’s own retrospective testimony establishes a specific intellectual debt, not personal teaching. The later methodological endorsement is jointly authored with Jean-Claude Schmitt; it neither rejects all earlier scholarship nor certifies a complete reading of the cited Bloch works.
primary_locators: 1986 printed p.20, paragraph beginning “Nous avons donc été amenés à nous tourner vers Marc Bloch”
1996 printed p.361, paragraphs beginning “Marc Bloch écrivait” and “Et la méthode”

proposals.relationship: Le Goff identifies Braudel’s placing geographical space at the center of historical inquiry as an inspiring resource during his formation.
proposals.evidence_note: Primary retrospective testimony, not an inference from institutional succession. It concerns the spatial approach exemplified by La Méditerranée; it does not claim Le Goff adopted every Braudelian thesis.
primary_locators: 1986 printed p.20, “Braudel et Marx,” first two paragraphs

proposals.relationship: Le Goff invokes Febvre’s unconventional biographies as precedents when explaining his own Saint Louis project.
proposals.evidence_note: His retrospective account names Luther and Marguerite de Navarre despite Annales’ reputation for avoiding biography. This bounded methodological precedent is not a claim of personal mentorship.
primary_locators: 1997 printed p.338, paragraph beginning “Paradoxalement l’idée me vint”

proposals.relationship: Nora’s invitation to introduce O’Connell’s collection brought Le Goff to Saint Louis’s reported words, an encounter he identifies in explaining the origin of his biographical project.
proposals.evidence_note: Le Goff’s own opening account credits an editorial invitation and the resulting source encounter. O’Connell compiled the texts; Nora did not write them or supply the whole biography’s method. The retrospective approximate project date is not a precisely dated commission.

proposals.relationship: Le Goff questions Duby’s exaggerated instrumentalization and silence of medieval women while praising his recovery of their historical presence.
proposals.evidence_note: In his own answers to Klapisch-Zuber, Le Goff balances criticism with praise. Her questions are not automatically attributed to him; no inferred personal motives or wholesale rejection of Duby is asserted.
primary_locators: Interview §§13 and24: exaggeration of instrumentalization and silence; §§18–22 and46: counterbalancing praise
